records.title: ux(vscode): actionable message when agent-loop commands run from the palette
records.release_claim: commands requiring a diagnostic target tell palette users to invoke Quick Fix on a RIPR diagnostic
records.reason: Useful recovery guidance but independent of the underlying code-action and packet-authority contracts; it may defer if the packaged extension preserves accurate unavailable messages.
records.non_claim: Palette invocation without a diagnostic target still performs no repair, verification, or receipt action.

records.title: fix(vscode): add ripr.showOutput to activation events
records.release_claim: the Show Output recovery action activates the extension before first use
records.reason: The command was registered and offered from warnings but was the only such command without activation metadata, making the advertised recovery path fail in a cold session.
records.non_claim: Activation does not resolve or start the server unless the invoked workflow requires it.

records.title: ux(vscode): surface the real server failure in the error popup
records.release_claim: server-resolution failures expose the bounded real cause and a copyable diagnostic instead of only a generic unavailable message
records.reason: HTTP, checksum, missing-asset, and mirror failures are otherwise hidden in the Output channel, undermining first-use and recovery claims. Clipboard rejection remains guarded.
records.non_claim: The popup does not bypass Workspace Trust, origin policy, checksum verification, or server-resolution failure.

records.title: docs(vscode): mark bundled-server resolution as not yet shipped
records.release_claim: the editor resolution order does not describe an unimplemented bundled-server branch as current behavior
records.reason: Release and agent documentation must match the selected packaging model; users otherwise chase a binary path that no current VSIX contains.
records.non_claim: The selected release does not bundle the native server unless a later exact-candidate packaging change explicitly does so.

records.title: docs(vscode): document Remote-SSH install location and Web non-support
records.release_claim: the extension runs where the workspace lives for Remote-SSH, Containers, and WSL, and Web or virtual workspaces remain unsupported
records.reason: Server installation, process location, and workspace-kind limitations materially affect the packaged extension contract and troubleshooting path.
records.non_claim: The extension does not support browser-only VS Code or virtual workspaces in this release.
